ordered_diagnoses: Follicular thyroid carcinoma with local invasion

facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s presented with swelling of the manubrium
12 years after resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe through a midline sternotomy approach
The swelling was slightly tender and had increased in size markedly over the month prior to presentation
Swelling noted over the manubrium, which was slightly tender
lytic lesion replacing the manubrium measuring 2.7 × 4.4 × 5.8 cm
residual right goiter
The posterior aspect is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Revealed follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion
Hematoxylin-eosin stained specimens showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae
previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter 12 years ago

concepts.why: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells and the infiltration of thyroid follicles into adjacent bone trabeculae suggest metastatic disease.
The history of previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter and the current findings of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion suggest a possible recurrence of the disease.

aliases: Follicular thyroid cancer with local spread
concepts.why: The close proximity of the lytic lesion to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein, along with the infiltration of thyroid follicles into adjacent bone trabeculae, suggest local invasion of the tumor.

rationales.F02: History of thyroid surgery increases the likelihood of recurrence or metastasis.
rationales.F05: Lytic lesion in the manubrium is highly suggestive of metastatic or invasive disease.
rationales.F06: Residual goiter increases the likelihood of recurrent disease.
rationales.F07: Proximity to major vessels increases the likelihood of local invasion.
rationales.F08: Follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion are highly suggestive of metastatic or invasive disease.
rationales.F09: Infiltration of thyroid follicles into bone trabeculae is highly suggestive of invasive disease.
